newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher while calls on pork belly futures ranged from 0.500 cent lower to 0.300 higher, livestock analysts said.

Steady to higher cash hog indications for Wednesday and another advance in pork cutout values were expected to encourage carryover demand in hog futures. Hog runs have been on the light side and the higher trend in wholesale pork prices has prompted packers to raise bids for hogs, analysts said.
There is growing speculation of increased export business with Japan, they said.
The market also looks strong technically after posting a reversal on the weekly charts, they added.

Some analysts look for initial pressure in pork bellies following Tuesday's CME Out-of-Town Report. The report showed a net in-movement of 1.117 million lbs, above the high end of both analyst and trader expectations.

However, others expected that report to be pushed aside by estimates for a bullish Cold Storage report this Friday. Higher cash belly prices and lighter-than-year-ago hog slaughter were also cited as early supporting factors, they said.

Early analyst estimates on USDA's Cold Storage report for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses as of May 31 ranged from 53.7 million to 57.7 million lbs. This compares with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for the period of 54.98 million lbs set in 1973.
